Commentary.Commentary: The players are back in the field with the match officials for the run chase. Kashyap Prajapati and Jatinder Singh are the two openers for Oman while Mark Watt will bowl the first over.
...RUN CHASE...

Right then, Scotland will be the happier of the two sides at the halfway mark. They would fancy themselves to defend down this total. On the other hand, Oman have a daunting total in front to overhaul. Can the Oman batters chase this down and create more history? Let's find out after we return for the chase.

The man of the moment, Brandon McMullen is in for a flash interview. He says it feels special to get the maiden ton for the country. Adds that the ball kept a bit low and was swinging so the plan was to keep playing every delivery on its merit and it worked out. Adds that his dad gave him special advice to play in the V and it worked out well. Also adds that they need to be nice and aggressive and get the 10 wickets as simple as that.

For Oman, Bilal Khan and Fayyaz Butt started off well giving away just 35 runs but the lack of support for Bilal has helped the Scottish side to post a big total. Moreover, the spinners were taken to the cleaners as well. That said, Oman did well to pull things back in the last ten overs but they still have a challenging total to chase. Bilal Khan was outstanding as he scalped a fifer. Fayyaz Butt took a couple of wickets and Jay Odedra took a wicket too.

A classic ODI is on offer between these two sides as we are halfway to the game with Scotland scoring 320 in their quota of 50 overs. The game started off in the best fashion for Oman as they got rid of Christopher McBride in the first over itself. Bilal Khan and Fayyaz Butt were swinging the ball like a pendulum early on but the arrival of Brandon McMullen on the crease changed the momentum of the game in the favour of the Scottish side as he scored quickly and put up an aggressive approach in the middle muddle. McMullen was well helped by skipper Richie Berrington who batted at a brisk pace too to reach his half-century before eventually getting out on 60. Towards the end, Mark Watt played a quickfire cameo of 25 runs to help Scotland cross the 300-run mark. Brandon McMullen was the star of the show for Scotland as he got past his maiden century in less than run a ball before perishing on 136.

Scotland though have notched up two wins out of two and have done so in exciting fashion as well. In their first game, they came back from the claws of defeat to outclass neighbors Ireland in a thrilling encounter. Then, against UAE, the middle order yet again put on a show with the bat as Richie Berrington scored a fabulous hundred to take his side to a solid total. The bowlers then rounded off a clinical display as they bowled out the opposition for just 171 runs allowing Scotland to take firm control of second place in their group behind Sri Lanka. Oman have also been pretty good defeating Ireland in their opening game and then following it up with a victory over UAE as well. It was in their last game against Sri Lanka that they were dealt a heavy blow as they were bundled out for just 98 runs. They would want to bounce back against a rampant Scottish side and a win in this game would propel them over their opponents in the points table which could be crucial in the context of their tournament. All in all, this is set up to be a fascinating encounter but Scotland do have a bit of an edge and momentum as well. Can Oman find a way to get the win? Or will Scotland continue their hot streak?
